definitions.gloss: to diversify; to become diverse; to become more varied
definitions.explanation: To increase in variety or become more heterogeneous. Used for trends, markets, lifestyles, and needs becoming more varied over time.

examples.japanese: ニーズが{多様化|たようか}している。
{働|はたら}き{方|かた}が{多様化|たようか}してきた。
examples.english: Work styles have become more diverse.

examples.japanese: {消費者|しょうひしゃ}の{価値観|かちかん}が{多様化|たようか}する{中|なか}で、{企業|きぎょう}は{新|あたら}しい{戦略|せんりゃく}を{求|もと}められている。
examples.english: As consumer values diversify, companies are being asked to develop new strategies.

notes:
{多様化|たようか}する is formed from {多様|たよう} (diverse) + {化|か} (change into), meaning to become diverse. It is a buzzword in business, media, and social commentary, describing how modern society, markets, and lifestyles are becoming increasingly varied. Primarily intransitive.

USAGE:
- ～が{多様化|たようか}する: ~ becomes more diverse (most common)
- ～を{多様化|たようか}する: to make ~ more diverse (transitive, less common)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ニーズの{多様化|たようか}: diversification of needs
- {価値観|かちかん}の{多様化|たようか}: diversification of values
- {働|はたら}き{方|かた}の{多様化|たようか}: diversification of work styles
- {多様化|たようか}に{対応|たいおう}する: to respond to diversification

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {多様|たよう}な: diverse — the base adjective, describes a state rather than a process
- {複雑化|ふくざつか}する: to become more complex — focuses on increasing complexity rather than variety
- {変化|へんか}する: to change — general change without the specific nuance of increasing variety
